title: Strict-localization base change for an ind-etale affine map
statement:
Let $A\to B$ and $A\to C$ be homomorphisms of commutative rings, with $B$ ind-etale over $A$ [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. Put $Y=\operatorname{Spec}B\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}C$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Xi\to Y$ be a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point], and denote its projections by $\bar b$, $\bar c$ and their common image in $\operatorname{Spec}A$ by $\bar a$. For strict localizations [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], the functorial morphisms [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality] induce a canonical isomorphism
$$Y_{(\bar y)}\longrightarrow (\operatorname{Spec}B)_{(\bar b)}\times_{(\operatorname{Spec}A)_{(\bar a)}}(\operatorname{Spec}C)_{(\bar c)}.$$
Its composites with both projections are the functorial maps of strict localizations; in particular it commutes with the structural maps to $Y$. No finiteness condition on $A\to C$ and no algebraicity condition on $\Xi$ over any of the image residue fields is required.

proof.text: Use strictHenselizationMap_existsUnique, the pointed interface to strict-henselization functoriality, for the four arrows of the affine pullback. Rewrite the geometric-point equalities to identify their endpoints. Apply the same uniqueness statement to the composite map to Spec A: both composites l ≫ u and m ≫ v satisfy its structural square and pointed evaluation equation, so the square commutes.

For any affine S and geometric point s, take the global affine chart S.isoSpec.inv. The affine-chart ind-etaleness theorem, with the coordinate map obtained by Spec.preimage, says that the strict-local structural map is pro-affine-etale. The equivalence proAffineEtale_Spec_iff and invariance under the affine-spectrum isomorphism translate between ring and scheme formulations. For a pointed map h over an affine pro-affine-etale f, composition and cancellation in the source-library proAffineEtale API make h pro-affine-etale: h followed by the target structural map equals the source structural map followed by f. This is precisely the ind-etale relative-map argument, expressed on affine schemes.

Equip both strict-local coordinate rings with their local structures from strictHenselizationLocalStructure. Evaluation into Ω is local: its factor through the relative separable closure is surjective, hence local, and the inclusion of that closure into Ω is a field map, hence local. The pointed evaluation equality says evaluation of the target is evaluation of the source composed with Spec.preimage h. Locality therefore cancels to give locality of the ring map. Its ind-etaleness gives weak etaleness, so Olivier gives bijectivity; full faithfulness of Spec turns this into IsIso h.

Apply the preceding affine pointed-map argument to Spec.map f and to its base change pullback.snd. The original fibre product is affine by Mathlib pullback instances; base-change stability of proAffineEtale supplies the second input. Thus u and m are isomorphisms. Let c = pullback.lift l m of the commuting strict-local square. Its composite with pullback.snd u v is m; the second projection is an isomorphism because u is, so c is an isomorphism. Take asIso c. Its two projection equations are pullback.lift_fst and pullback.lift_snd. Pullback extensionality and the structural squares give compatibility over Y. The same extensionality, followed by Iso.ext, proves uniqueness.
